title: Serial Communication Link
plain: The engine computer has lost or is getting bad communication with another computer in the car over a data link.
symptoms: Several other warning lights may come on
Transmission may go into limp mode

causes.name: Damaged wiring or loose connector on the communication network
Low battery voltage or poor grounds
Faulty module on the network
Faulty engine computer

checks: Test the battery and check main grounds
Scan every module for communication (U) codes to see which one is missing
Inspect network wiring and connectors, especially near the computers
fix: Usually a wiring, connector or power and ground repair; sometimes a faulty module.

title: Internal Control Module Memory Check Sum Error
plain: The engine computer's self-check found that its stored program doesn't add up correctly, meaning its memory may be corrupted.
symptoms: Engine may not start or may stall
Runs poorly or goes into limp mode

causes.name: Failing engine computer
Corrupted software from an interrupted or failed reprogramming
Low battery voltage during programming
Water damage at the computer

checks: Test the battery and charging system
Check the computer power and ground connections
Try reprogramming the computer with the latest software
fix: Reprogram the computer first; replace and program it if the code returns.

title: Control Module Programming Error
plain: The engine computer is not programmed, or its programming did not complete correctly.
symptoms: Engine may not start or may run poorly

causes.name: Computer not programmed after replacement
Interrupted or failed software update
Low battery voltage during programming
Internal computer fault

checks: Ask whether the computer was recently replaced or updated
Reprogram with a battery maintainer connected
fix: Usually reprogramming the computer; replace it only if programming will not take.

title: Internal Control Module Keep Alive Memory (KAM) Error
plain: The computer's keep-alive memory, which stores learned settings, lost its data. This often happens after the battery is disconnected or goes dead.
symptoms: Idle or shifting may feel off until the computer relearns
Often shows up after battery work

causes.name: Battery recently disconnected, replaced or run dead
Loose or corroded battery terminals
Blown fuse or poor connection on the computer constant-power feed
Failing engine computer

checks: Find out whether the battery was recently disconnected or died
Check the battery terminals and the computer constant-power fuse
Clear the code and see if it returns after a few drives
fix: Often goes away after fixing the battery connection and clearing the code; replace the computer only if it keeps coming back with good power.

cost.job: Clean battery terminals and check computer power feed

title: Internal Control Module Random Access Memory (RAM) Error
plain: The engine computer's self-test found an error in its working memory (RAM).
symptoms: Possible reduced power, stalling or no start
Other warning lights may come on

causes.name: Low battery voltage or poor power or ground connections at the computer
Internal computer fault
Computer software that needs an update or reprogramming
Water damage or corrosion at the computer connector

checks: Test the battery and charging system
Check the computer power and ground circuits and connectors
Check for manufacturer software updates or service bulletins
fix: Fix any power or ground problem first; otherwise the computer may need reprogramming or replacement (a new one usually must be programmed to the car).

title: Internal Control Module Read Only Memory (ROM) Error

Check the computer power and ground circuits and connectors
Check for manufacturer software updates or service bulletins
fix: Fix any power or ground problem first; otherwise the computer may need reprogramming or replacement (a new one usually must be programmed to the car).

title: Control Module Processor
plain: The engine computer's self-test found a problem with its own processor, the chip that runs the engine.

causes.name: Internal engine computer fault
Low system voltage or poor power and ground connections
Computer software that needs an update
Water damage or corrosion at the computer connector
Shorted sensor or actuator dragging down computer circuits

checks: Test the battery and charging system
Check the computer power and ground circuits and connectors
Check for software updates or service bulletins
Clear the code and see if it returns
fix: Fix any voltage or ground problem first; if the code returns, the computer usually needs reprogramming or replacement.

title: Control Module Performance

fix: Fix any power or ground problem first; otherwise the computer may need reprogramming or replacement (a new one usually must be programmed to the car).

title: Control Module VSS Output "A"
plain: The engine computer sends a vehicle speed signal ("A") to other systems, and it found a problem in that output circuit.
symptoms: Speedometer, cruise control or other speed-based features may not work

causes.name: Short or open in the speed output wiring
Faulty module that receives the speed signal
Faulty vehicle speed sensor input
Engine computer fault

checks: Inspect the speed output wiring and connectors
Check for speed sensor codes and fix those first
fix: Usually a wiring repair; sometimes a receiving module or the engine computer.

title: Internal Control Module Accelerator Pedal Position Performance

causes.name: Internal computer fault
Erratic or faulty accelerator pedal sensor signal
Low voltage or poor power and ground connections
Computer software that needs an update

checks: Test the battery and charging system
Check the computer power and ground circuits and connectors
Check for manufacturer software updates or service bulletins
fix: Fix any power or ground problem first; otherwise the computer may need reprogramming or replacement (a new one usually must be programmed to the car).

title: Control Module Vehicle Options Error
plain: The engine computer isn't set up with the right options for this vehicle, often after it was replaced.
symptoms: Engine may not start or features may not work right

causes.name: Replacement computer not configured for the vehicle
Wrong computer part number installed
Interrupted programming
Internal computer fault

checks: Confirm the computer part number matches the vehicle
Have the computer configured or programmed with a dealer-level scan tool
fix: Usually programming or configuring the computer for the vehicle.

title: Fuel Injector Control Module Performance
plain: The separate module that fires the fuel injectors, mostly on diesels, is not performing correctly.

causes.name: Low voltage reaching the injector control module
Faulty fuel injector control module
Weak batteries
Wiring or connector problem

checks: Test the batteries and charging system
Check the module supply voltage while cranking and running
Inspect the module connectors
fix: Usually a repaired or new fuel injector control module, after confirming good battery and charging voltage.
examples: Ford 6.0L Power Stroke diesels are known for injector control module failures

title: Fuel Injector Control Module Relay Control
plain: The computer found a problem, such as a broken connection, in the circuit it uses to control the fuel injector control module relay. This part powers the module that fires the fuel injectors.

causes.name: Faulty fuel injector control module relay
Broken wire or loose or corroded connector
Blown fuse or failed relay
Computer driver circuit fault (rare)

checks: Inspect the fuel injector control module relay wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
Check related fuses and relays
Test the fuel injector control module relay with a meter or scan tool and compare with spec
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new fuel injector control module relay if it tests bad.

title: TCM Processor
plain: The transmission computer's self-test found a problem with its own processor.
symptoms: Transmission stuck in one gear or limp mode

causes.name: Low battery voltage or poor power or ground connections at the computer
Internal computer fault
Computer software that needs an update or reprogramming
Water damage or corrosion at the computer connector

checks: Test the battery and charging system
Check transmission computer power and ground connections
Check for transmission computer software updates
fix: Fix any power or ground problem first; otherwise the transmission computer needs reprogramming or replacement.

title: ECM / TCM Incompatible
plain: The engine computer and transmission computer don't match each other, usually after one was replaced or reprogrammed.
symptoms: Transmission may be in limp mode
Engine may not start on some vehicles

causes.name: Wrong engine or transmission computer installed
Computer not programmed after replacement
Mismatched software versions
Internal computer fault

checks: Ask whether either computer was recently replaced or updated
Confirm part numbers and update software on both computers
fix: Usually programming both computers with matching software, or installing the correct part.

title: Starter Relay Circuit
plain: The computer found a problem, such as a broken connection, in the circuit it uses to control the starter relay. This part switches power to the starter when you turn the key or press start.
symptoms: Clicking with no crank, or cranking only sometimes

causes.name: Faulty starter relay
Broken wire or loose or corroded connector
Blown fuse or failed relay
Computer driver circuit fault (rare)

checks: Inspect the starter relay wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
Check related fuses and relays
Test the starter relay with a meter or scan tool and compare with spec
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new starter relay if it tests bad.

title: Starter Relay Circuit Low
plain: The computer sees lower voltage than expected in the circuit that controls the starter relay, often from a wire shorted to ground. This part switches power to the starter when you turn the key or press start.
symptoms: Clicking with no crank, or cranking only sometimes

causes.name: Control wire shorted to ground
Faulty starter relay
Corroded connector
Computer driver circuit fault (rare)

checks: Inspect the starter relay wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
Check related fuses and relays
Test the starter relay with a meter or scan tool and compare with spec
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new starter relay if it tests bad.

title: Starter Relay Circuit High
plain: The computer sees higher voltage than expected in the circuit that controls the starter relay, often from a wire shorted to power or a failed part. This part switches power to the starter when you turn the key or press start.
symptoms: Clicking with no crank, or cranking only sometimes

causes.name: Control wire shorted to power
Faulty or shorted starter relay
Corroded connector
Computer driver circuit fault (rare)

checks: Inspect the starter relay wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
Check related fuses and relays
Test the starter relay with a meter or scan tool and compare with spec
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new starter relay if it tests bad.

title: Alternative Fuel Control Module KAM Error
plain: On vehicles that run on natural gas or propane, the fuel system module lost its stored learned settings.
symptoms: May switch to gasoline or run poorly on the alternative fuel

causes.name: Low voltage or poor power and ground at the module
Internal alternative fuel module fault
Module software that needs updating

checks: Test the battery and module power and grounds
Clear the code and see if it returns
fix: Fix any power problem; otherwise the alternative fuel module may need replacement.

title: Alternative Fuel Control Module RAM/ROM Error
plain: On vehicles that run on natural gas or propane, the fuel system module found an error in its internal memory.
symptoms: May switch to gasoline or run poorly on the alternative fuel

causes.name: Low voltage or poor power and ground at the module
Internal alternative fuel module fault
Module software that needs updating

checks: Test the battery and module power and grounds
Check for module software updates
fix: Usually reprogramming or replacing the alternative fuel module.
